comment: Success is validated through conformance, adoption and coverage metrics. No goal or metric addresses whether the receiving actor acts appropriately on exchanged information. A message can arrive complete, coded and conformant, and still leave the receiver unable to decide what to do. Moreover, 'capture once, use many times' assumes reuse is free; in practice information must be transformed to fit each receiver's role and context (informational metamorphosis), and this transformation is neither designed nor governed.

public.text: Success is validated through conformance, adoption and coverage metrics. No goal or metric addresses whether the receiving actor acts appropriately on exchanged information. A message can arrive complete, coded and conformant, and still leave the receiver unable to decide what to do. Moreover, 'capture once, use many times' assumes reuse is free; in practice information must be transformed to fit each receiver's role and context (informational metamorphosis), and this transformation is neither designed nor governed.
public.suggestedRevision: Add to §4.4 (and reference from §3.7.5) an explicit pragmatic outcome measure: periodic, scenario-based assessment of whether receiving actors (clinicians, community health workers, administrators, clients) take the appropriate next action on the basis of exchanged records. Additionally, design and govern receiver-appropriate views of shared records (role- and context-specific transformations). Position appropriateness-of-action as the ultimate validation criterion of the seven goals.
